title_human: CDT L(2,chi_-3) reconstruction, Franke Layer-B completion, and L(3,chi_5) six-sheet no-go

claims.statement: The CDT reconstruction of L(2,chi_-3) (V9 integration patch) recovers a filtration collapse 14 -> 3 -> 1 with tau_F = 191/49, tau_hor = 27/80, and tau_ad = 16603/3920, built on top of the exact source identification D^2 B_CDT = (1-8V^2) E_{3,chi_-3,1} and D^2 C_CDT = (1-V^2) E_{3,1,chi_-3}.
claims.object: L(2,chi_-3) arithmetic-holonomy reconstruction, adelic Layer C
claims.notes: Framed as reproducing the 'fine arithmetic cost' of CDT's known successful irrationality proof, but presented as a modeling/reconstruction exercise, not an independently verified new theorem; depends on trunk's still-open adelic Layer C formalism (see trunk).

claims.statement: The 'boundary-completed Franke/Layer-B' theorem is claimed complete: the Franke critical kernel, orientation resolution, and full cusp-boundary kernel are now treated as successive exact linear stages, resolving the open sequence 0 -> K_full -> E_(Crit,Res) -> C_crit (+) C_partial -> ... that the trunk had flagged as the single most important remaining classification theorem.
claims.notes: Status 'proved' is the thread's own framing ('done', 'no longer left as a conjectural programme item'); no independent verification found here. See trunk for the original open problem statement this resolves.

claims.statement: For the L(3,chi_5) genus-one/six-sheet programme, the source calculation reduces the viable level-20 realization to the unique line G* = S + 4V^2 S - 32V^4 S on X_0(20) \ {Q,3Q,4Q}, with base 2Q; the three cusps Q,3Q,4Q cannot be removed because the relevant boundary matrix has determinant 289/32 =/= 0.
claims.notes: Cited as already established in an uploaded source document (L3_CHI5_SIX_SHEET_COMPLETION_ATTEMPT); not independently re-derived in this message.
Explicit uniformization computed in this message as a 'useful simplification.'

claims.statement: The level-10 realization of the L(3,chi_5) six-sheet route fails the CDT entry condition unconditionally via an elementary one-term theta estimate: after normalizing to z_0 = 1/2 - i, tau_0 = i K(z_0)/K(1-z_0) satisfies -0.533 < Re(tau_0) < -0.532, 0.846 < Im(tau_0) < 0.847, giving |theta_3(tau_0)| < 0.9958, hence r_u < (pi/2)(0.847)(0.9958)^4 < 1.309 < e^{117/400}, so log r_u < 117/400.
claims.notes: Presented as a rigorous elementary no-go, stronger than the earlier numerical conformal-radius estimate from the same thread (log r_x ~ 0.26736 computed earlier, also below the 117/400=0.2925 threshold).

claims.statement: The level-20 route is closed by a computer-assisted monotone-submetric certificate: an explicit metric sigma = exp(u_s + v_20 - 3/40)|dz| (u_s an exact two-cusp theta model, v_20 a degree-20 Fourier correction) gives sigma(1/3) = 4.2677223281830188268..., while the most favorable arithmetic threshold is Omega_1 e^{-117/400} = 4.2162003523116518836..., a margin of 0.05152197587..., establishing log r_x < 117/400 with explicit error budgets |delta v|,|delta u_s| <= 10^-7.
claims.notes: Thread explicitly states this is a 'robust computer-assisted certificate' but not yet publication-grade: 'the only remaining publication-level computational refinement is a directed-rounding Arb/MPFI-style rerun; the present implementation uses very conservative explicit error budgets rather than a true outward-rounded interval library.'

claims.statement: General monotone entry obstruction theorem: if X is the actual continuation surface, X subset Y, and sigma is any curvature-<=-1 conformal pseudometric on Y, then rho_X(z_0) >= rho_Y(z_0) >= sigma(z_0), so r_x(X,z_0) <= 2|x'(z_0)|/sigma(z_0), and sigma(z_0) <= e^{tau_ad}/(2|x'(z_0)|) already constitutes a complete no-go for arithmetic holonomy without needing the exact hyperbolic metric or full CDT energy.
claims.object: General arithmetic-holonomy no-go criterion (adelic Layer C)
claims.notes: Derived from Ahlfors-Schwarz-type monotonicity of hyperbolic metrics under domain inclusion; presented as a new general theorem of the theory, distilled from the level-10/level-20 computations.

claims.statement: Finite-place mixed invariant theorem: if the local extension matrix is Phi_E = (Phi_V, 0; kappa_p, 1), changing the splitting by v sends kappa_p -> kappa_p + (Phi_V - 1)v, so the canonical object is not kappa_p itself but its class [kappa_p] in coker(Phi_V - 1), and this class satisfies the Hecke-equivariance identity [kappa_p(C nu)] = C[kappa_p(nu)], giving q_p[kappa_p(C nu)] = lambda_C q_p[kappa_p(nu)] on a one-dimensional eigenquotient q_p where C acts by lambda_C.
claims.object: Finite-place Hecke-Eisenstein functoriality (adelic Layer C, p-adic extension theory)
claims.notes: Builds on Sprang's syntomic elliptic polylogarithm and Bannai-Kings' ordinary-locus p-adic Eisenstein description (external literature, cited via arXiv). The remaining open piece is explicitly flagged: constructing the canonical Dirichlet regulator quotient q_{p,r,chi} and proving V_d -> d^{-r} there together with q_{p,r,chi}[kappa_p(nu_{r,chi})] = E_p(r,chi) L_p(r,chi).

claims.statement: Summary status at end of chain: the L(3,chi_5) six-sheet programme is closed at both natural levels (level 10 via elementary theta no-go, level 20 via monotone submetric no-go), i.e. 'perfect Layer-B purification does not imply Layer-C Diophantine viability' for this construction.
claims.notes: This is the thread's own summary framing of the two preceding no-go results, not an independent additional claim.
